1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night
In Peñaseca it had been raining for three days. That spring, Lucía Romero's older sister had left for Madrid, and since then Lucía had been running the small village apothecary alone.
At nightfall, she closed the shutters, counted the day's earnings, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely gone to bed when someone knocked loudly on the door downstairs. A man's voice asked, "Is anyone there?"
On the threshold stood a young man soaked to the bone, his left arm wrapped in a bloodstained cloth. He said his name was Diego Lobo and that he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need someone to treat me," Lobo said quietly. "I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred reales be enough?"
He took a letter wrapped in waxed paper from his jacket. "This letter has to reach the monastery of San Blas before the eighteenth of May."
For Lucía, healing that wound was child's play, but the letter troubled her.
Even so, she refused his money and simply said, "Tomorrow at dawn I'll take it to the mountain."
2: At daybreak they set out. Lucía carried a basket on her back with bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the slope they ran into old Tomás Gil, who was chopping firewood. He set down his axe and told them in a low voice that the previous afternoon three strangers had asked at the entrance to the village about a wounded young man.
"Take the path, Lucía," said Tomás Gil. "The main road isn't safe." Lucía thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Lucía went in front, planting her feet firmly with every step. Lobo followed her in silence.

By noon it had stopped raining, the fog slowly lifted, and in the distance the roof of the San Blas monastery appeared. A nun was waiting at the door, Sister Inés, who was in charge of greeting visitors.
Sister Inés took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting for this letter for 2 years."
Lobo said to Lucía, "I owe you my life." Lucía smiled. "Then, the next time you come, fix the roof of the apothecary for me." Lobo stayed at the monastery.
At dusk, Lucía came down the mountain alone. By the time she got home it was already night; she lit the lamp and sat behind the counter for a long time.
